blocks.text: HEBREWS · STEP BY STEP · ITS SHAPE · SIDE BY SIDE · SIDE BY SIDE
The argument
How the sermon makes its case: Christ better at every step, read against the Law it fulfils.
STEP BY STEP
Better than…
Each step of the argument, and what it is better than.
a Son, God's last word — God spoke in many ways through the prophets; in these last days he has spoken by his Son. Hebrews 1:1–2
a more excellent name — "So much better than the angels." The first "better" of the letter. Hebrews 1:4 Hebrews 1:5–14 Hebrews 2:5–9
more glory: the builder, not the house — Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house; Christ as a Son over it. Hebrews 3:3 Hebrews 3:5–6
the rest Joshua did not give — The KJV reads "Jesus" in 4:8, the Greek form of the name Joshua. Hebrews 4:8–9

a priest for ever, after the order of Melchizedek — Many priests died in turn; he continues for ever. "The less is blessed of the better." Hebrews 5:4–6 Hebrews 7:7 Hebrews 7:11 Hebrews 7:19 Hebrews 7:23–25
a better covenant, on better promises — 8:6 uses "better" twice. Hebrews 7:22 Hebrews 8:6–13
the true tabernacle, in heaven itself — "A greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands." Hebrews 8:2 Hebrews 9:11 Hebrews 9:24
better sacrifices: his own blood, once for all — "How much more shall the blood of Christ…" Hebrews 9:12–14 Hebrews 9:23 Hebrews 10:10–14

a better possession, country and resurrection — A better and lasting substance, a heavenly country, a better resurrection, "some better thing for us". Hebrews 10:34 Hebrews 11:16 Hebrews 11:35 Hebrews 11:40
the blood that speaks better things — Abel's blood cried out from the ground (Gen 4:10); Jesus' blood speaks better things. Hebrews 12:24

The Greek word for "better" (kreittōn) appears 13 times in 12 verses, and other comparisons ("more excellent", "more glory", "how much more") carry the same idea. The ladder follows the order of the argument, from the prophets to the blood of Jesus. Davidson and Dods describe the same sequence. Hebrews 1:4 Hebrews 12:24 [7][11]

SIDE BY SIDE
The Day of Atonement and Hebrews 9
Leviticus 16 beside Hebrews 9. Click a ribbon to keep it.

Hebrews 9 reads Christ's work through the Day of Atonement. The yearly entry of the high priest, alone and with animal blood, is set against Christ's single entry with his own blood. The carcasses burned "without the camp" in Lev 16:27 return in Heb 13:11–13, where Jesus suffers outside the gate. Leviticus 16:27 Hebrews 13:11–13
SIDE BY SIDE
Melchizedek
Genesis 14 beside Hebrews 7. Click a ribbon to keep it.

Hebrews draws on two passages: the meeting in Genesis 14 and the oath of Psalm 110:4, "Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek", quoted at 5:6, 7:17 and 7:21. Westcott notes that the writer reads the record of Scripture, including its silences, rather than the historical man. He passes over the bread and wine, presenting Melchizedek as a priest who blesses rather than one who sacrifices. Psalms 110:4 Hebrews 5:6 Hebrews 7:17 Hebrews 7:21 Genesis 14:18 [4]
